podcast.body: This song was a massive cultural phenomenon, topping the charts for 10 consecutive weeks from November 21, 1981, to January 23, 1982, spanning Thanksgiving, the holidays, and nearly Valentine's Day. Olivia Newton-John recorded it after Rod Stewart and Tina Turner passed on it, initially unsure about its daringly suggestive lyrics, which included lines like "There's nothing left to talk about unless it's horizontally." Her manager ultimately convinced her to record it, and its catchy tune, fitness-themed video (directed by Brian Grant), scorching guitar solo by Steve Lukather of Toto, and Olivia's playful yet sexual performance made it a career-defining and era-defining hit, closely associated with the 80s aerobics craze and MTV's early days. Foreigner's "Waiting For A Girl Like You" was blocked from the number one spot by "Physical" for nine weeks. "Let's get physical, physical. All I can, physical. Let's get physical. Let me fight it down."

This song was a number one hit that notably blocked Foreigner's "Waiting for a Girl Like You" from reaching the top spot on the Hot 100 for part of its ten-week run at number two. "parked behind the number one hits physical by Olivia Newton-John."

podcast.body: This song was the Billboard year-end number one for 1982, catching "lightning in a bottle" as it appeared on radio the same year Jane Fonda's workout book ignited America's aerobics and fitness craze. It spent a record 10 weeks atop the Hot 100 from November 1981 through January 1982 and was a bigger hit in the United States than in her native UK or Australia. "Physical spent a record 10 weeks atop the hot 100 from November 1981 through January 1982."
